inputs.root_cause: FF6-EVENT-000294 fixed 3 call sites where `except OraError` missed OraValidationError/OraLimitError. This event audited every other FF6 format's own error hierarchy (nrrd, xliff, ubl, safetensors, ipynb) and found all 5 use multiple inheritance so every format-specific exception subclass IS ALSO the format's own base error class -- ora was the sole outlier, with OraValidationError(FormatValidationError) and OraLimitError(ResourceLimitError) declared as siblings of OraError rather than subclasses. This was the actual root cause, not merely 3 missed except clauses.
inputs.obligation_targeted: None -- architecture correctness improvement preventing recurrence of FF6-EVENT-000294's own bug class, not an obligation closure.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: Verified MRO resolves cleanly with no conflicts; a new structural regression test (test_ora_validation_and_limit_errors_are_also_ora_errors) asserts the subclass relationship directly so a future edit reverting it fails immediately, independent of any specific call-site symptom.
inputs.regression_tier: full ora suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Audited every other FF6 format's own errors.py: nrrd/xliff/ubl all declare Parse/Write/Validation error subclasses via multiple inheritance, e.g. `class NrrdParseError(FormatParseError, NrrdError)` -- BOTH a cross-format FormatParseError AND the format's own NrrdError. safetensors's own validate() catches all exceptions broadly (no risk). ipynb's own hierarchy is single-inheritance but internally consistent (every subclass inherits IpynbError directly). Only ora's errors.py declared OraValidationError/OraLimitError as siblings of OraError, not subclasses -- the actual root cause of FF6-EVENT-000294's bug.
2. Grepped every `except.*Ora.*Error` site across ora's own src/ tree (5 total) to confirm no other latent instances of the bug existed beyond the 3 already fixed -- confirmed clean.

3. Changed errors.py: `OraValidationError(FormatValidationError, OraError)` and `OraLimitError(ResourceLimitError, OraError)`, matching the established cross-format multiple-inheritance pattern. Updated both classes' own docstrings and the module docstring to explain why, referencing the bug this prevents recurring.

4. Verified the MRO resolves without conflict (Python's C3 linearization) via direct inspection: OraValidationError.__mro__ = [OraValidationError, FormatValidationError, OraError, FormatParseError, FormatFactoryError, Exception, BaseException, object]; OraLimitError.__mro__ analogous.
5. Verified validate() still behaves correctly end-to-end for both a non-ZIP source and the thumbnail-unreadable fixture from the immediately preceding commit.

6. Added a dedicated structural regression test asserting `issubclass(OraValidationError, OraError)` and `issubclass(OraLimitError, OraError)` directly -- a root-cause guard, not just a symptom guard, since the 3 call-site fixes already have their own symptom-level regression tests from the prior commit.
7. Ran mypy --strict (clean), ruff (clean), the full ora suite (336 -> 337 passed, +1), and the 6-format regression (3654 -> 3655 passed, +1, 0 failed).
